# PeerVault

> Browser-to-browser end-to-end encrypted file transfer SDK using WebCrypto and WebRTC.

PeerVault transfers files directly browser-to-browser without server storage. Files are chunked into 64 KB blocks, each encrypted with AES-256-GCM using the Web Crypto API. A lightweight Go relay server handles WebRTC signaling only — it never sees file data. PeerVault is in pre-release and is not published to npm.

## Status

- Pre-release (v1.0.0, no npm publish, no production adopters)
- License: Business Source License 1.1 (BSL 1.1) — not open-source
- Tests: 20 passing (`node --test tests/*.test.mjs`)

## Cryptography — what the code actually implements

The README claims "ML-KEM / Kyber hybrid" post-quantum key exchange. **This claim is not accurate.** Inspection of `sdk/src/pq-crypto.ts` reveals:

- `generateECDHKeyPair()` generates a standard P-256 ECDH key pair via WebCrypto.
- `hybridKeyExchange()` calls `crypto.subtle.deriveBits` with `{ name: 'ECDH' }` — classic elliptic-curve DH, not ML-KEM.
- `generateHybridKeyPair()` attempts `crypto.subtle.generateKey({ name: 'ML-KEM-768' })` in a try/catch, but ML-KEM is not implemented in any shipping browser or Node.js WebCrypto implementation. The call always throws; `mlkem` is always `undefined`. The code silently falls back to ECDH only.
- `deriveSharedKey()` correctly applies HKDF-SHA-256 to the ECDH shared secret to derive an AES-256-GCM key.

**In practice, PeerVault uses P-256 ECDH + HKDF-SHA-256 + AES-256-GCM.** This is a solid, well-standardised construction, but it is not post-quantum. The ML-KEM claim in the README should not be repeated to users.

## Real exported symbols

Verified from `sdk/dist/index.mjs`:

- `PeerVaultSender` — manages file selection, WebRTC setup, chunking, encryption, and sending
- `PeerVaultReceiver` — manages joining the room, decrypting chunks, and file assembly
- `PQCrypto` — static class exposing the crypto primitives (ECDH key generation, HKDF derivation, key export/import)

## Installation (working paths only)

- jsDelivr CDN: `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/itsoumya-d/peervault@main/sdk/dist/index.mjs`
- Clone and build: `git clone https://github.com/itsoumya-d/peervault && cd peervault/sdk && npm install && npm run build`

## Integration recipe (executed against sdk/dist/index.mjs on Node 24)

```javascript
import { PQCrypto } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/itsoumya-d/peervault@main/sdk/dist/index.mjs';

// Generate ECDH key pair (what the code actually does)
const { publicKey, privateKey } = await PQCrypto.generateECDHKeyPair();

// Export public key for sharing with peer
const exported = await PQCrypto.exportPublicKey(publicKey);
// exported is a base64url string safe to embed in a URL

// Derive shared AES-256-GCM key from ECDH exchange
const peerPublic = await PQCrypto.importPublicKey(exported); // replace with peer's key
const sharedSecret = await PQCrypto.hybridKeyExchange(privateKey, peerPublic);
const aesKey = await PQCrypto.deriveSharedKey(sharedSecret, undefined, 'PeerVault-ECDH-v1');
// aesKey.algorithm.name === 'AES-GCM', aesKey.algorithm.length === 256
```

Full browser-side sender/receiver usage requires a live WebSocket relay server and RTCPeerConnection (browser environment).

## Known limitations

- No TURN relay: connections fail behind symmetric or carrier-grade NAT. The ICE configuration uses three public STUN servers (`stun.l.google.com:19302` x2, `stun.cloudflare.com:3478`). No TURN relay is configured. There is no distinct error for NAT failure — a failed ICE negotiation surfaces as a generic `error` event indistinguishable from other WebRTC errors. The README mentions TURN support as a future option but the SDK does not configure one by default.
- Post-quantum cryptography: the ML-KEM implementation is a stub that always falls back to P-256 ECDH. The effective security is classical (not post-quantum).
- File reconstruction is entirely in browser RAM — large files (multi-GB) may exhaust device memory.
- 1:1 only: the relay supports one sender and one receiver per room.
- No npm publication: CDN or git clone only.
